svg.title: ALA one-shot and interactive execution flows
svg.desc: One-shot execution creates a new ALA runtime and temporary workspace for one request and removes them afterward, so no conversation continues into the next process. Interactive execution retains one runtime, workspace, selected coding backend and native continuation until the user exits.
svg.text: One-shot execution
One operating-system process handles exactly one composed request.
1. Start ALA and load current state
Parse input, load config and repositories, detect available backends.
2. Build runtime and route the request
Use direct MainAgent execution or select the coding-agent path.
3. Coding-agent path creates a fresh workspace
Bind it at /workspace and mount current task skills and folders.
Run one detected backend inside a new Bubblewrap child process.
The direct model path skips this workspace.
4. Normalize and deliver the result
Result uses stdout or the selected file; diagnostics remain separate.
5. Close runtime and delete temporary workspace
The process exits after this request.
Native continuation and conversation are not reused by the next process.
A later one-shot invocation starts again from current config, repositories
and explicitly mounted persistent folders.
Interactive execution
One ALA process retains runtime state across multiple terminal prompts.
1. Start ALA and build one runtime
Load initial config, repositories, backend discovery and slash commands.
2. Read a prompt or handle a local command
Folder, repository, model and web-search changes affect later turns.
3. Execute within the retained runtime
The coding workspace is created lazily and then reused.
The first coding backend is pinned; its native continuation is retained.
Each backend turn still starts a sandboxed native child process.
4. Return result and wait for the next line
The ALA process, MainAgent and session workspace remain active.
Next prompt
Reuse conversation, pinned backend, continuation and workspace files.
/quit or process end: close runtime and remove workspace
